content: 1. Say-Barber-Miller syndrome is characterized by short stature, valvular heart disease, and distinctive facial features. 2. Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome, type 2, involves skeletal dysplasia, intellectual disability, coarse facial features, and mental retardation. 3. Spastic diplegia of the infantile type is a condition marked by increased muscle tone and stiffness, primarily affecting the legs. 4. Spinal muscular atrophy, type I, with congenital bone fractures, is a severe neuromuscular disorder that includes progressive muscle weakness and fragile bones. 5. Spondylohypoplasia with arthrogryposis and popliteal pterygium is a condition involving underdeveloped vertebrae, joint contractures, and webbing behind the knees. 6. Stargardt macular degeneration is a genetic eye disorder leading to progressive vision loss. It may be associated with absent or underdeveloped corpus callosum, intellectual disability, and dysmorphic features. 7. Stratton-Parker syndrome is a rare genetic condition with specific clinical manifestations. 8. Teebi-Shaltout syndrome is a genetic disorder with distinct phenotypic features. 9. Tel Hashomer camptodactyly syndrome is characterized by permanently bent fingers and other associated anomalies. 10. Thiele syndrome involves thin ribs, tubular bones, and dysmorphic features. 11. Thiolase deficiency is a metabolic disorder caused by an enzyme defect, leading to issues in fatty acid metabolism. 12. Trigonocephaly with a bifid nose and acral anomalies is a craniofacial condition involving a triangular-shaped forehead, split nose, and limb abnormalities. 13. Trigonocephaly with ptosis and coloboma includes craniofacial abnormalities, drooping eyelids, and defects in eye structure. 14. Trisomy 10 mosaicism is a chromosomal disorder where some cells have an extra copy of chromosome 10, leading to various developmental abnormalities. 15. Trisomy 14 mosaicism syndrome involves the presence of an extra copy of chromosome 14 in some cells, causing growth and developmental issues. 16. Trisomy 21 mosaicism is a form of Down syndrome where only some cells have an extra copy of chromosome 21. 17. Turner mongolism polysyndrome is an outdated term that may refer to a combination of Turner syndrome and other syndromic features. 18. Unusual facial features, osteosarcoma, and malformation syndrome describe a condition involving distinct facial characteristics, bone cancer, and congenital anomalies. 19. Van der Woude syndrome is a genetic disorder characterized by cleft lip, cleft palate, and lip pits. 20. Van der Woude syndrome 2 is a variant of the condition with similar features. 21. Velofacioskeletal syndrome involves abnormalities of the palate, facial structure, and skeleton. 22. Von Voss-Cherstvoy syndrome is a rare genetic condition with specific clinical features. 23. Waaler-Aarskog syndrome is a genetic disorder characterized by short stature, facial abnormalities, and skeletal anomalies. 24. Weaver syndrome is a condition involving rapid growth, distinctive facial features, and developmental delay. 25. Wiedemann-Tolksdorf syndrome is a rare genetic disorder with specific phenotypic characteristics. 26. Zellweger-like syndrome without peroxisomal anomalies is a condition resembling Zellweger syndrome but without the typical peroxisomal defects. This list represents a detailed enumeration of various syndromes and conditions, each with its own unique clinical presentation and underlying genetic or developmental causes.
